tasks.acceptance: The CLI reports plans and evidence clearly, does not silently claim/close, and can always show the native task source.

tasks.title: Compose one Caf CML Brew workflow
tasks.work: Use visible local CML to select exact binding, policy refs, context profile, verification, closeout, and recovery without live task fields.
tasks.acceptance: Typed/CML-HX canonical bytes match and invalid refs, multiple authorities, provider-native fields, and missing evidence fail closed.

tasks.title: Complete cafetera-4vzs.81 with shared Brew
tasks.work: Run a real Caf development task through selection, exact context, agent delivery, verification, evidence/close, receipt, and refreshed graph.
tasks.acceptance: The existing issue receives the provider-use manifest, value comparison against direct bd, clean recovery proof, and second-provider evidence.

tasks.title: Prove Brew removal and direct BeadsHX fallback
tasks.work: Remove or disable Brew from a fixture while retaining full direct bdhx and TaskPort operation.
tasks.acceptance: No task data or essential BeadsHX operation depends on Brew, and the same database remains valid.

milestones.title: Dogfood, cutover, 1.0, and continuing upstream control
milestones.objective: Move from evidence to daily use without placing the owner workflow at avoidable risk, then establish durable maintenance.
exit_gate: Dogfood progresses through read-only, disposable, non-critical, selected daily, and primary cutover stages.
A full rollback drill succeeds.
BeadsHX 1.0 ships with complete evidence and exact compatibility scope.
Upstream tracking is operational.
forbidden: No big-bang replacement.
No removal of upstream fallback before a successful cutover/rollback drill and approved soak.
No future upstream merge directly into a release claim without requalification.

tasks.title: Run shadow read-only dogfood
tasks.work: Run bdhx reads beside upstream bd on copied and selected read-only real workspaces and compare every result.
tasks.acceptance: No unexplained mismatch occurs across the agreed event count and time window; no write path is enabled.

tasks.title: Run disposable write dogfood
tasks.work: Use full workflows on throwaway repositories, including concurrency, sync, backup, restore, migration, and crash recovery.
tasks.acceptance: All failures are recoverable and upstream can continue every database without repair.

tasks.title: Run non-critical repository dogfood
tasks.work: Make bdhx the default for one non-critical repository with automatic verified backups and immediate upstream fallback.
tasks.acceptance: The repository completes the accepted soak/event threshold with no data-loss, corruption, or blocked workflow defect.

tasks.title: Run selected daily workflow dogfood
tasks.work: Use bdhx for the owner-ranked daily profile across selected projects while retaining exact fallback and monitoring fallback usage.
tasks.acceptance: All fallbacks are eliminated or intentionally excluded before release; restore drills succeed from real dogfood backups.

tasks.title: Perform the primary-workflow cutover drill
tasks.work: Back up, verify, switch, complete representative work, simulate failure, roll back to upstream, then switch forward again.
tasks.acceptance: The drill preserves all task state/history and produces a clear operator runbook with measured recovery time and steps.

tasks.title: Publish BeadsHX 1.0
tasks.work: Release signed, provenance-backed artifacts, source, generated source, SBOM, licenses, compatibility report, install docs, migration docs, and recovery docs.
tasks.acceptance: All M00-M21 gates are green at the release commit and the release page makes divergences/platform limits visible.

tasks.title: Permit the optional bd alias
tasks.work: After the approved soak, provide an explicit install option or wrapper that exposes bdhx as bd while preserving a direct upstream binary name.
tasks.acceptance: The alias is reversible, reports BeadsHX identity, and cannot strand the user without an upstream-compatible fallback.

tasks.title: Establish upstream tracking and rebase policy
tasks.work: Define scheduled discovery, delta classification, security intake, compatibility target upgrades, conflict handling, attribution, and release branches.
tasks.acceptance: Every upstream commit/release delta enters the program ledger and cannot silently change the compatibility target.

tasks.title: Create the next-target upgrade procedure
tasks.work: Automate command/schema/dependency diff, corpus refresh, migration matrix expansion, compiler impact report, and staged requalification for later Beads releases.
tasks.acceptance: A dry run against the next available upstream delta produces a bounded issue graph and does not modify the 1.0 compatibility claim.

tasks.title: Close the program with retained recovery paths
tasks.work: Archive evidence, close or re-scope remaining issues, retain exact oracle builds/source tags, verify clean repositories, and document continuing owners.
tasks.acceptance: The project is maintainable without hidden local state, and upstream bd, backup restore, native debug, and Brew removal remain tested escape hatches.
